exact_statement_tex: [Albanese equivalence in positive characteristic]\label{thm:alb} Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$, let $X/k$ be smooth projective connected of dimension $n$, let $A/k$ be an abelian variety, and let $1\leq i\leq n$. If $Z\in\CH^i(A\times X)$ is integral and $u_Z=0$ as a homomorphism of integral groups, then, for every prime $\ell\ne p$, its transpose induces the zero map \[ {}^tZ_*:H^{2(n-i)+1}_{\et}(X,\Q_\ell(n-i)) \longrightarrow H^1_{\et}(A,\Q_\ell). \] The corresponding map with $\Z_\ell$ coefficients is also zero. The conclusion need not hold if the premise is weakened to $u_Z\otimes\Q=0$.

exact_statement_tex: [Universal range modulo algebraic equivalence]\label{thm:range} The following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For $0\leq i\leq n/2$, the map $L^{n-2i}:A^i(X)\to A^{n-i}(X)$ is surjective for every smooth projective complex $n$-fold and every ample $L$ if and only if $i=0$ or $2i=n$. In those two cases it is an isomorphism. For each $1\leq i<n/2$ there is an $X$ for which the source is finite-dimensional and the target infinite-dimensional, for every ample $L$. \item For $0\leq r\leq n$, each of the following properties holds for every such $n$-fold in codimension $r$ if and only if $r\in\{0,1,n\}$: injectivity of the rational cycle class map; coincidence of algebraic and numerical equivalence after tensoring with $\Q$; finite-dimensionality of $A^r(X)$; finite generation of $(\CH^r(X)/\CH^r(X)_{\alg})/\mathrm{torsion}$. \item If $n=2m$ and $P^m_L(X)=\ker(L:A^m(X)\to A^{m+1}(X))$, then \[ q(x,y)=(-1)^m\deg(xy) \] is positive semidefinite on $P^m_L(X)$ and \[ \rad(q)=\ker\bigl(L:G^m(X)\to G^{m+1}(X)\bigr). \] Thus positive definiteness is exactly the injectivity of this last map. It holds universally for $m=0,1$. No assertion for all $m\geq2$ follows from parts~(i) and~(ii). \end{enumerate}

exact_statement_tex: [Bounds for the Jacobian factor obstruction]\label{thm:scalar} Over every algebraically closed field, in every characteristic, an abelian variety of dimension $g>0$ satisfies \[ s_J(A)\mid(2g-1)!. \] If $g\leq3$, it also satisfies $s_J(A)\mid\delta(A)$. More precisely, \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \dim A&\text{bound}\\\hline 2&s_J(A)\mid\gcd(2,\delta(A))\\ 3&s_J(A)\mid\gcd(6,\delta(A)). \end{array} \] Consequently an abelian surface with an ample line bundle of odd Euler characteristic is a direct factor of a product of Jacobians. The same holds for a threefold if its ample Euler characteristics have greatest common divisor prime to six.

exact_statement_tex: \label{lem:induction} For every integer $i\geq1$ there is a smooth projective $(2i+1)$-fold $X_{2i+1}$, embedded as a smooth divisor in a smooth projective $(2i+2)$-fold $R_{2i+2}$ with a direct sum of Tate motives, such that $G^r(X_{2i+1})$ vanishes except for $r=i+1$, where it is infinite-dimensional. Every other $A^r(X_{2i+1})$ is finite-dimensional.

exact_statement_tex: [Integral Matsusaka calculation]\label{lem:scalar} Let $X/k$ be an abelian variety of dimension $d>0$ and $L$ a line bundle with $\theta=c_1(L)$. If an integral curve cycle has rational $\ell$-adic cohomology class, for some $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, \[ \alpha=n\frac{\theta^{d-1}}{(d-1)!}, \] then $n\chi(X,L)\in I_J(X)$.

exact_statement_tex: \label{lem:prym} For a principally polarized abelian variety $(B,\Xi)$ of dimension $1\leq h\leq5$ over an algebraically closed field, there is an integral curve cycle with class \[ 2\frac{\xi^{h-1}}{(h-1)!},\qquad\xi=c_1(\Xi), \] in rational $\ell$-adic cohomology for $\ell$ different from the characteristic. In particular $2\in I_J(B)$.
